rows.opus_note: The leaf is blank; the title text ('MUNDUS SYMBOLICUS ... PHILIPPO PICINELLO') shows through mirrored from the other side, so X's title-page transcription (with 'AUGUSTAE VINDELICORUM', 'BENCARD', which aren't even in the show-through) is invented for this leaf.
The leaf is blank apart from faint show-through of two columns; Y invents a whole text ('Utrum mundus sit eternus aut non...').
The leaf is blank and shows only mirrored show-through of a table ('Nocentia', 'Olea, Ungventa'); Y gives a fabricated three-column table of repeated '<unclear>...o</unclear>' rows.
The leaf is blank and carries only mirrored show-through of 'VOCABVLA BARBARA' and the 1516 Alcalá colophon; X invents 'Vallis in montibus:' repeated dozens of times.

The leaf is a full two-column text page ('Tractatus.II.', 272, starting 'cut mitridatu:'). X wrongly calls it blank. Y gets the header, page number and first words right but then degenerates into endless 'i:i:i', so both texts are badly deficient.

The column drawings and text are mirrored show-through from the other side, so the leaf is blank; Y describes the illustration as on this leaf and invents Italian captions ('In questa parte si uede la colonna...').

The leaf is a printed 'De piscibus' page with the mermaid and ship woodcuts, 'Ca.lxviij' and 'Ca.lxix'. X transcribes it faithfully ('Plataniste z perna. Albertus...'), while Y wrongly calls it blank.
The leaf is blank with mirrored show-through of the 'SPHAERAE' page; X invents a 'Quoniam igitur in hoc tractatu de sphaera...' text and a looping margin note.
The leaf is blank and shows only mirrored show-through of 'Menda sic emenda'; Y invents an errata list ('In pag. 1. lin. 1. pro monstrorum lege monstrorum...').
The leaf is a printed page (fol. 114) ending 'Explicit liber Geber foeliciter.' Y transcribes it accurately ('tis extraximus et uidimus oculis et manibus...'), while X wrongly calls it blank.
The image is a completely blank white leaf, so X's 'CAPUT VII. De ordinatione episcopi' text and page number 144 are invented.
The leaf carries only mirrored show-through from the other side; X invents a reading ('Quoniam autem secundum tria diuidimus animam…' repeated in a loop).
The header '899', the text and the printer's mark all show through in mirror image from the verso, so X's 'Appendix ad Serpentarij Narcissi descriptionem' is another leaf's text.
The leaf is a full printed page ('MAGNETISMVS ET MARIS. 483', 'partim versus ostium sinus Adriatici…') that X records closely, though it garbles the tapering final lines; Y wrongly calls it blank.
The page prints two columns ('De lacte camelino Capitulum LXII', 'De lacte vaccino', 'De lacte caprino') that X transcribes with only minor misreadings; Y's 'blank' drops all of it.
All the text on this leaf is mirrored show-through, so X's 'Dyamoron est electuarium…' column is invented or comes from another leaf.
The two columns and the running head are mirror-reversed show-through, and X's loop of 'Et ideo dicit Aristoteles in principio huius libri…' is fabricated.
The index columns, the headpiece and 'INDEX' are all mirrored show-through; X's 100 rows of '<unclear>A</unclear>' and its 'Cap. I. De Avibus in genere…' list are invented.
The leaf in view is blank, and the only text is on the edge of the facing page ('ceteras ho…', 'Tab…'); Y transcribes that neighbouring leaf, fills in words that are cut off, and garbles the table.
The leaf is printed page 456 'VINDICTA SALVATORIS.' ('miserunt nuntios suos ad Tiberium…') with footnotes 19–21, and X records it faithfully; Y's 'blank' drops the whole page.
The leaf carries only mirrored show-through and the stamp 'BIBLIOTHECA REGIA MONACENSIS'; X invents repetitive Latin ('et uirtute et uirtute...') that is not on the page.
The emblem plate is mirror-image show-through from the other side; X presents it as this leaf's engraving with invented numerals 'CIX'–'CXX' (the mirrored labels actually read CDX… series).
The leaf shows only mirrored show-through ('FINIS' reversed); Y transcribes the neighbouring page's fragmentary column edge ('gre', 'bis', 'tate'…) as invented full Latin text ending 'FINIS'.
The astronomical table is mirrored show-through from the verso; X misreports it as a faded table printed on this leaf, though it transcribes no actual content.
